name: Jumla Sign Language
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Sapkota, Sharada. Phonological Parameters in Nepali Sign Language. MA thesis, Tribhuvan University. hdl:20.500.14540/20016.
sources.note: Closest open sign-phonology work from the same department (on Nepali SL, not Jumla SL); useful only as a template for what a TU sign-phonology thesis covers and to check whether it mentions Jumla SL. Not a source for Jumla SL itself.

sources.citation: Hurlbut, Hope M. (2012). A Lexicostatistic Survey of the Signed Languages in Nepal. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2012-021. Dallas: SIL International. 23 pp. OCLC 896400475.
sources.note: Glottolog's subclassification source for juml1239 and the only published primary fieldwork on Jumla SL (wordlist comparison with Jhankot, Ghandruk and NSL varieties). Open on sil.org but the site's JS challenge blocked downloading by automated download; expected to contain no prosody, but it should be read to confirm and to harvest its bibliography.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority (2007). Change Request 2007-030: Request for New Language Code Element — Jumla Sign Language [jus]; requester Hope Hurlbut (SIL); adopted 2008-01-14. 7 + 5 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic identification form only: Deaf of Jumla (Chandannath VDC) monolingual in their own sign language, distinct from Nepali Sign Language; no dictionary, grammar or published source listed under 'Knowledge from published sources'.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (English and Nepali), 'Jumla Sign Language'; sister pages Nepali/Jhankot/Ghandruk Sign Language
sources.note: Nothing; stubs citing Ethnologue only (8 monolingual signers, 2005). NSL page lists Jumla SL among four 'village sign languages' of Nepal, 'insufficiently studied'.

sources.citation: Timilisena, Davendra (2015). Jumla Sign Language. MA thesis, Central Department of Linguistics, Tribhuvan University, Kathmandu.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained

sources.note: The only descriptive work on the language (Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description 'phonology or text collection'); if any statement on sign-phonological prominence/prosody exists it would be here. Not in TU eLibrary; would need a copy from TU's Central Department of Linguistics or the author.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid record for juml1239 (Hammarström et al.) and its three reference records (687313 Timilisena 2015; 549559 Hurlbut 2012; 500588 ISO 2007)
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: Nothing. Glottolog's most extensive description ranking: Timilisena 2015 = 'phonology or text collection' (listed by Glottolog as a study of one feature); Hurlbut 2012 = 'a wordlist or less' (overview; comparative; lexicostatistics, 23 pp.); ISO change request = overview. Subclassification note: 'Lexicostatistically quite distinct from other sign languages in Nepal (Hurlbut 2012)'.
